sections.text_helper: Section 24.4.8 "OPAMP operating modes" in chapter 24 (Operational amplifier (OPAMP)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 730.
sections.section_content:
OPAMP can be configured to different operating modes or use cases, through:
• OPAMP control registers
• GPIOx_MODER registers, configuring the I/Os selected as OPAMP inputs and output
• COMP registers, selecting a COMP input channel when the operational amplifier
output is redirected to the COMP
• External components, defining the gain, bias, or filtering parameters
The principal operating modes are:
• Stand-alone operational amplifier
• Follower
• Programmable-gain amplifier (PGA)
Refer to the following subsections for details and for different PGA flavors.
Through the OPAINTOEN bit of the OPAMP control/status register (OPAMP_CSR), the
operational amplifier output OUT can be connected to the I/O pin selected as OPAMP
output (default) or to an internal COMP input channel. However, the latter option cannot be
used when the operational amplifier output on the pin is required.
The OPAHSM bit (0 by default) allows increasing the operational amplifier speed (slew rate).
The USERTRIM bit can enable writing to the input offset trimming register, to allow
modifying the by-default factory trimming values by the user.
The impedance of the input signal must be low enough to prevent the OPAMP input current
from creating a voltage drop in the source, thus altering the input voltage. Refer to the
electrical characteristics section in the datasheet for further details.
Standalone operational amplifier
For this use, ensure the following settings.
• Select a pin for the INP input (as opposed to a DAC output), with VP_SEL[2:0] and
VPS_SEL[2:0] bitfields.
• Set the VM_SEL[1:0] bitfield to 0X, to ensure that a pin is selected for the INM input.
• Clear OPAINTOEN bit, to direct the operational amplifier output to the OPAMP_VOUT
pin.
With these settings, the INP, INM inputs, and the OUT output of the operational amplifier are
connected to pins and to no other internal structure.
Note: The OPAMP_CSR, OPAMP_TCMR, and GPIOx_MODER registers in their default state
configure OPAMP as standalone operational amplifier, with normal speed, factory offset
trimming values, and with OPAMP_VINP0 and OPAMP_VINM0 selected for INP and INM,
respectively. The OPAMP is disabled so the OUT and OPAMP_OUT are in high-Z state.
Once enabled, OPAMP operates as a standalone operational amplifier, with the gain,
filtering, and biasing determined by external routing and components.
For this use, the operational amplifier output OUT must be directed to the OPAMP_VOUT
pin, and not to the internal COMP channel.

Follower
To use OPAMP as a follower with an internal feedback, set the following bitfields as
indicated:
• VM_SEL[1:0] to 11 and VMS_SEL to 1, to loop the operational amplifier output back to
its inverting input INM
• VP_SEL[1:0] and VPS_SEL[1:0] according to the pin or internal DAC output to select
for the noninverting input INP
Once enabled, the operational amplifier buffers the voltage selected on its noninverting
input INP.
Note: The GPIOs corresponding to OPAMP_VINMy are free for another use.
In this mode, OPAMP takes two pins if a pin is selected for INP noninverting input. It takes a
single pin if an internal DAC output is selected for INP noninverting input (on instances
supporting this). Refer to Section24.3.

Programmable-gain amplifier
When OPAMP is configured as a programmable-gain amplifier (PGA), the internal resistor
divider with a programmable resistor value determines the amplifier gain. Refer to the
datasheet for the values of the internal resistors.
The following sections describe different PGA flavors.
Noninverting PGA
To use OPAMP as a noninverting PGA without filtering, set the following bitfields as
indicated:
• VM_SEL[1:0] to 10 and VMS_SEL to 0, to connect the resistor divider middle point to
the inverting operational amplifier input
• PGA_GAIN[4:0] and PGAS_GAIN[4:0] to 00XXX, with XXX according to the desired
positive gain
• VP_SEL[1:0] and VPS_SEL[1:0] according to the pin or internal DAC output to select
as noninverting operational amplifier input
Once enabled, OPAMP outputs a voltage that corresponds to the selected input pin voltage
multiplied by the selected gain value.
Note: To avoid saturation, keep the product of the input voltage and the selected gain value below
VDDA.

Noninverting PGA with filtering
To use OPAMP as a noninverting PGA with filtering, set the following bitfields as indicated:
• VM_SEL[1:0] to 10 and VMS_SEL to 0, to connect the resistor divider middle point to
the inverting operational amplifier input
• PGA_GAIN[4:0] and PGAS_GAIN[4:0] to 10XXX, with XXX according to the desired
positive gain
• VP_SEL[1:0] and VPS_SEL[1:0] according to the pin or internal DAC output to select
as noninverting operational amplifier input
Once enabled, OPAMP outputs a voltage that corresponds to the selected input pin voltage
multiplied with the selected gain (for static signals).
External components connected between the OPAMP_VOUT pin and the OPAMP_VINM0
pin are put in parallel with the internal programmable resistor. For example, connecting a
capacitor CF as shown in Figure160 has a filtering effect equivalent to CF’ of the same
capacitance. The gain for dynamic signals then also depends on the signal frequency and
the cutoff frequency of the filter.
For this use, the operational amplifier output OUT must be directed to the OPAMP_VOUT
pin and not to the internal COMP channel.

Noninverting PGA with external bias, or inverting PGA
To use OPAMP as a noninverting PGA with external bias or as an inverting PGA, set the
following bitfields as indicated:
• VM_SEL[1:0] to 10 and VMS_SEL to 0, to connect the resistor divider middle point to
the inverting operational amplifier input
• PGA_GAIN[4:0] and PGAS_GAIN[4:0] to 01XXX, with XXX according to the desired
positive gain
• VP_SEL[1:0] and VPS_SEL[1:0] according to the pin or internal DAC output to select
as noninverting operational amplifier input
For the signal on the selected OPAMP_VINPy pin, OPAMP operates as a noninverting
amplifier with the selected positive gain. The OPAMP_VINM0 pin is used as a reference
(bias).
For the signal on the OPAMP_VINM0 pin, OPAMP operates as an inverting amplifier with
the selected negative gain. The selected OPAMP_VINPy pin is used as a reference.
Note: The final gain depends upon the output impedance of the source connected to the
OPAMP_VINM0 pin.
For this use, the operational amplifier output OUT must be directed to the OPAMP_VOUT
pin, and not to the internal COMP channel.

Inverting or noninverting PGA with external bias or/and filtering
To use OPAMP as a noninverting PGA with external bias, or as an inverting PGA with
filtering, set the following bitfields as indicated:
• VM_SEL[1:0] to 10 and VMS_SEL to 0, to connect the resistor divider middle point to
the inverting operational amplifier input
• PGA_GAIN[4:0] and PGAS_GAIN[4:0] to 11XXX, with XXX according to the desired
positive gain
• VP_SEL[1:0] and VPS_SEL[1:0] according to the pin or internal DAC output to select
as noninverting operational amplifier input
For the signal on the selected OPAMP_VINPy pin, OPAMP operates as a noninverting
amplifier with the selected positive gain. The voltage on the OPAMP_VINM0 pin is used as a
reference (bias).
For the signal on the OPAMP_VINM0 pin, OPAMP operates as an inverting amplifier with
the selected negative gain. The voltage on the selected OPAMP_VINPy pin is used as a
reference (bias). The output impedance of the biasing voltage source impacts the total gain.
In both cases, any external components connected between the OPAMP_VOUT pin and the
OPAMP_VINM1 pin are put in parallel with the internal programmable resistor. For example,
connecting a capacitor CF as shown in the following figure has a filtering effect equivalent to
CF’ of the same capacitance. The gain for dynamic signals then also depends on the signal
frequency and the cutoff frequency of the filter.
For this use, the operational amplifier output OUT must be directed to the OPAMP_VOUT
pin and not to the internal COMP channel.
